source_fields.title: Internship Applications Open
source_fields.summary: The Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Undergraduate Internship Program applications open today. Learn more at sustainability.tamu.edu.
source_fields.description:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open October 6, 2025 – November 9, 2025 at sustainability.tamu.edu.

Want to see the real-world impact of the Aggie Green Fund? You’re invited to the AGF Project Showcase, where past grant recipients will share how their projects are making Texas A&M a more sustainable place.

This is your opportunity to hear directly from the students, faculty, and staff who are turning innovative ideas into reality. You’ll learn about a range of projects and from every corner of our campus. 

Join us to get inspired, ask questions, have a snack, and celebrate the incredible work being done to create a greener campus.

source_fields.summary: Environmental Health & Safety provide Stream Clean as a service opportunity for campus members to volunteer their time cleaning litter and debris from campus streams. All students, faculty and staff are welcome to participate, and any student organization can register their group.
source_fields.description:
All Aggies who participate will earn FIVE entries into our CSM Grand Prize Giveaway with winners announced November 7.

Volunteers should wear long pants and closed-toed shoes, as you may be walking through tall grass and weeds. Each volunteer will be supplied with a pair of gloves, a litter picker, and a garbage bag to assist with picking up trash and debris. White Creek on West Campus will be the focus area.

Participant Arrival Time/Location: 7:45 a.m. in Parking Lot 97 off John Kimbrough Boulevard. You will sign in, pick up equipment and listen to a safety briefing before beginning stream clean activities.

To sign up, go to https://signup.com/go/mcxOMta.

  • Click on the “Sign Up” button (green button)
  • Add your email address, participant name, number of spots (total number of participants), phone number and select your t-shirt size from the dropdown menu.
  • After completing, click “Save” and “Done” (green button).

Signing up a Group?

If you are adding an entire group, please add each person’s name individually, along with their contact information and t-shirt size. Select “Save and Add Another Person” (blue button) for each additional person’s information. This enables everyone to receive updates about the event, as well as any weather-related cancellations.

source_fields.summary: The Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Undergraduate Internship Program applications open today. Learn more at sustainability.tamu.edu.
source_fields.description:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open March 17th, 2026 – April 14th, 2026 at sustainability.tamu.edu.

title: Is Clean Energy Actually Clean?
thumbnail_alt: Celebrate Campus Earth Month with a globe graphic and OSCE logo

source_fields.title: Is Clean Energy Actually Clean?
source_fields.summary: We’re told that the future is clean energy, but what actually goes into it? In our talk, we dive into the world of energy transition minerals. Join us as we explore the complex trade-offs between global sustainability goals and the environmental realities of the mines that make them possible. From policy shifts to community impacts, we’re questioning if a truly clean future exists and what it will take to get there.

title: Caring for What Can’t Speak for Itself: Rights for Animals and Plants for Future Generations
thumbnail_alt: Celebrate Campus Earth Month with a globe graphic and OSCE logo

source_fields.title: Caring for What Can’t Speak for Itself: Rights for Animals and Plants for Future Generations
source_fields.summary: This talk examines our role as humans in environmental stewardship, the moral consideration we give to the interests of plants, animals, and future generations, all of which are unable to communicate their needs and interests to us. We argue that plants and animals have intrinsic value, or value within themselves, and that future generations deserve to see the beauty and aesthetics of the planet just as we have. This is based on the belief that all plants and animals have an interest in living, therefore worthy of our consideration in otherwise anthropocentric developments. By rethinking our role in environmental stewardship, we can begin making choices today that protect the world we leave behind.

Learn more and collect your Mason jar (or use your own!) from our office (Pavilion Suite 229) or from our team on April 1, 2026, 11 a.m.–2 p.m., Memorial Student Center, at the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment table!

  • Photo of your jar (or you & your jar) at the end of the week (5 points)
  • Reflection (5 points)
  • Additional photos (2points/unique photo MAX 10 - validity determined by OSCE Staff).

Take the Week Without Waste Challenge! Can you fit all your landfill waste into a Mason jar? Reduce, reuse, recycle, and rethink your habits—let’s see how small you can shrink your waste this week!

Learn more and collect your Mason jar (or use your own!) from our office (Pavilion Suite 229) or from our team on April 1, 2026, 11 a.m.–2 p.m., Memorial Student Center, at the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment table!

Document your participation in Week Without Waste by filling out this short form and earn up to 20 entries into our Earth Month Grand Prize Drawings. Submissions are due by April 11, 2026. Points can be earned as follows:

  • Photo of your jar (or you & your jar) at the end of the week (5 points)
  • Reflection (5 points)
  • Additional photos (2points/unique photo MAX 10 - validity determined by OSCE Staff).
To learn more about Campus Earth Month and our grand prize giveaway, see this link.

source_fields.description:

You can earn additional entries into our Earth Month giveaway by visiting our partner tables. Visit TX.AG/EarthMonth for a full list of our events, our giveaway prizes, and other opportunities to participate!

Earth Day is a feature event of our Campus Earth Month festivities, which serve as an arena for sustainability awareness and education. Our goal is to expose, educate, and empower attendees with the skills they need to be more sustainable - environmentally, socially, and economically.

source_fields.title: Hullabloom Fest - The Gardens
source_fields.summary: Celebrate the magic of spring — and the pollinators who make it possible — at The Gardens Hullabloom Fest! This joyful community event invites guests of all ages to explore the vibrant world of bees, butterflies, and other garden helpers through hands‑on activities, educational stations, and blooming seasonal displays.
source_fields.description:
Enjoy light refreshments, educational demonstrations, gardening resources, and family‑friendly crafts inspired by wings, petals, and everything in between. And of course we hope you’ll take part in what has become the highlight of the Hullabloom Fest: the butterfly release.

We will have a Sensory Free/Quiet Zone during the Hullabloom Fest for anyone who may want or need a quieter environment at any point during the event.

This event is a free event that is open to the community.

Schedule of Events

9:00 AM – Event Begins
Wander through The Gardens, visit table partners, grab a refreshment, and don’t forget to sign up to release a butterfly.
11:00 AM – Butterfly Release
We will begin handing out butterflies to those who signed up to release one at 10:45 am. Once all butterflies are handed out, we will gather and release on The Event Lawn.
11:30 AM – Event Ends
Thanks for joining us!

Unable to join us? No worries!

Here are a few ways you can still enjoy Spring out in The Gardens!

  • Download our scavenger hunt and explore The Gardens as you race to see who can find all of the items first!
  • Bring your camera for photos in front of our spring blooms wall at any time this April!
  • Create and enjoy one of these delicious spring recipes from Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service’s Dinner Tonight program.
    • Quick Chicken & Spring Vegetables
    • Peach & Blackberry Salad
    • Homemade Basil Pesto

Parking Information

Attendees can park for free in Lots 97 or 100c. More information about our parking options can be found at Parking and Transportation.

source_fields.title: Internship Applications Open
source_fields.summary:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open October 5, 2026 – November 2, 2026 at https://sustainability.tamu.edu/team/employment.html

source_fields.description: As the artificial intelligence industry grows, data center developments built by hyperscalers are rapidly expanding into residential backyards, creating environmental and socioeconomic strains for nearby communities. These mega-facilities consume vast resources—generating heavy upfront carbon emissions from concrete and steel construction while exacerbating local air, water, and noise pollution during operation. Furthermore, their power demands strain regional electricity grids, driving up residential utility bills and threatening power reliability. Addressing these localized community impacts requires corporate sustainability disclosures, global and local AI governance, and collaborative policy frameworks.
